---
title: "S3 Methods"
---

S3 methods for inspecting, summarizing, and using `bgms` and `bgmCompare`
model fits.

## print {#print}

Minimal console output for a fitted model.

### bgms

```r
print(x, ...)
```

| Argument | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `x` | An object of class `bgms`. |
| `...` | Ignored. |

Returns `x` invisibly.

### bgmCompare

```r
print(x, ...)
```

| Argument | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `x` | An object of class `bgmCompare`. |
| `...` | Ignored. |

Returns `x` invisibly.

## summary {#summary}

Posterior summaries and diagnostics for a fitted model.

### bgms

```r
summary(object, ...)
```

| Argument | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `object` | An object of class `bgms`. |
| `...` | Currently ignored. |

Returns an object of class `summary.bgms` with posterior summaries.

### bgmCompare

```r
summary(object, ...)
```

| Argument | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `object` | An object of class `bgmCompare`. |
| `...` | Currently ignored. |

Returns an object of class `summary.bgmCompare` with posterior summaries.

## coef {#coef}

Extract posterior mean coefficients.

### bgms

```r
coef(object, ...)
```

| Argument | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `object` | An object of class `bgms`. |
| `...` | Ignored. |

Returns a list with:

- `main` --- Posterior mean main-effect parameters. `NULL` for GGM models.
  For OMRF models: a numeric matrix (p x max_categories) of category
  thresholds. For mixed MRF models: a list with `$discrete` (threshold
  matrix) and `$continuous` (means matrix).
- `pairwise` --- Posterior mean pairwise interaction matrix. For GGM and
  mixed MRF models the precision matrix diagonal is included on the diagonal.
- `indicator` --- Posterior mean edge inclusion indicators (if available).

### bgmCompare

```r
coef(object, ...)
```

| Argument | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `object` | An object of class `bgmCompare`. |
| `...` | Ignored. |

Returns a list with:

- `main_effects_raw` --- Posterior means of raw main-effect parameters
  (variables x (baseline + differences)).
- `pairwise_effects_raw` --- Posterior means of raw pairwise-effect
  parameters (pairs x (baseline + differences)).
- `main_effects_groups` --- Posterior means of group-specific main effects
  (variables x groups), computed as baseline plus projected differences.
- `pairwise_effects_groups` --- Posterior means of group-specific pairwise
  effects (pairs x groups), computed as baseline plus projected differences.
- `indicators` --- Posterior mean inclusion probabilities as a symmetric
  matrix, with diagonals for main effects and off-diagonals for pairwise
  effects.

## predict {#predict}

Compute conditional probability distributions for one or more variables
given the observed values of other variables in the data.

### bgms

```r
predict(object, newdata, variables = NULL,
        type = c("probabilities", "response"),
        method = c("posterior-mean", "posterior-sample"),
        ndraws = NULL, seed = NULL, ...)
```

| Argument | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `object` | An object of class `bgms`. |
| `newdata` | A matrix or data frame with `n` rows and `p` columns. Must match the variables used in fitting. |
| `variables` | Character vector of names, integer vector of column indices, or `NULL` (all variables). |
| `type` | `"probabilities"` (full conditional distribution) or `"response"` (predicted category). |
| `method` | `"posterior-mean"` (use posterior means) or `"posterior-sample"` (average over draws). |
| `ndraws` | Number of posterior draws for `"posterior-sample"`. `NULL` uses all draws. |
| `seed` | Optional random seed. |

**Ordinal models**: For `type = "probabilities"`, returns a named list with
one matrix per variable (n rows x (num_categories + 1) columns). For
`type = "response"`, returns a matrix of predicted categories.

**GGM models**: For `type = "probabilities"`, returns a list with one matrix
per variable (n rows x 2 columns: `"mean"` and `"sd"`). For
`type = "response"`, returns conditional means.

**Mixed MRF models**: Returns a list combining both formats for discrete and
continuous variables.

When `method = "posterior-sample"`, predictions include an `"sd"` attribute
with the standard deviation across draws.

### bgmCompare

```r
predict(object, newdata, group, variables = NULL,
        type = c("probabilities", "response"),
        method = c("posterior-mean"), ...)
```

| Argument | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `object` | An object of class `bgmCompare`. |
| `newdata` | A matrix or data frame matching the original variables. |
| `group` | Integer specifying which group's parameters to use (1 to number of groups). Required. |
| `variables` | Which variables to predict (character, integer, or `NULL` for all). |
| `type` | `"probabilities"` or `"response"`. |
| `method` | `"posterior-mean"` (posterior mean parameters). |

Returns the same structure as `predict.bgms`, using group-specific
parameters obtained by combining baseline parameters and group differences.

## simulate {#simulate}

Generate new observations from a fitted model.

### bgms

```r
simulate(object, nsim = 500, seed = NULL,
         method = c("posterior-mean", "posterior-sample"),
         ndraws = NULL, iter = 1000,
         cores = parallel::detectCores(),
         display_progress = c("per-chain", "total", "none"), ...)
```

| Argument | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `object` | An object of class `bgms`. |
| `nsim` | Number of observations to simulate. Default: `500`. |
| `seed` | Optional random seed. |
| `method` | `"posterior-mean"` (single simulation) or `"posterior-sample"` (one dataset per draw, parallel). |
| `ndraws` | Number of posterior draws for `"posterior-sample"`. `NULL` uses all. |
| `iter` | Gibbs iterations for equilibration. Default: `1000`. |
| `cores` | CPU cores for parallel execution with `"posterior-sample"`. |
| `display_progress` | Progress bar style: `"per-chain"`, `"total"`, or `"none"`. |

If `method = "posterior-mean"`: a matrix (nsim x p). If
`method = "posterior-sample"`: a list of matrices, one per posterior draw.
For mixed MRF models, discrete columns contain integers and continuous
columns contain real values.

### bgmCompare

```r
simulate(object, nsim = 500, seed = NULL, group,
         method = c("posterior-mean"), iter = 1000, ...)
```

| Argument | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `object` | An object of class `bgmCompare`. |
| `nsim` | Number of observations to simulate. Default: `500`. |
| `seed` | Optional random seed. |
| `group` | Integer specifying which group to simulate from (1 to number of groups). Required. |
| `method` | `"posterior-mean"`. |
| `iter` | Gibbs iterations for equilibration. Default: `1000`. |

Returns a matrix (nsim x p) of simulated observations for the specified
group.

## simulate_mrf {#simulate_mrf}

Simulate observations from a Markov Random Field using user-specified
parameters (no fitted model needed).

```r
simulate_mrf(
  num_states,
  num_variables,
  num_categories,
  pairwise,
  main,
  variable_type = "ordinal",
  baseline_category,
  iter = 1000,
  seed = NULL
)
```

| Argument | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `num_states` | Number of observations to generate. |
| `num_variables` | Number of variables in the MRF. |
| `num_categories` | Integer or integer vector. Number of response categories on top of the base category (`1` = binary). |
| `pairwise` | Symmetric matrix of pairwise interactions. For continuous variables, this is the precision matrix (must be positive definite). |
| `main` | Main-effect parameters. For ordinal variables: a matrix of category thresholds. For continuous variables: a means vector. |
| `variable_type` | `"ordinal"`, `"blume-capel"`, or `"continuous"`. Can be a vector for mixed types (ordinal/Blume-Capel only). |
| `baseline_category` | Integer vector of baseline categories for Blume--Capel variables. |
| `iter` | Gibbs iterations for equilibration (ordinal only). Default: `1000`. |
| `seed` | Optional random seed. |

Returns a (num_states x num_variables) matrix of simulated observations.

For ordinal and Blume-Capel variables, the Gibbs sampler generates
observations from full conditional distributions. For continuous variables,
observations are drawn directly from $N(\mu, \Omega^{-1})$.
